prompt: Teach a polite greeting and ask the other person their name. Explain which part means hello.

expected.thai: สวัสดีค่ะ คุณชื่ออะไรคะ
expected.romanization: sà wàt dii khâ khun chʉ̂ʉ à rai khá

semantic_checklist: สวัสดี means hello, not ค่ะ.
ค่ะ ends the statement; คะ ends the question.

prompt: Teach me to introduce myself as Ann casually. Explain whether a pronoun is required.

expected.thai: ชื่อแอนค่ะ

semantic_checklist: ชื่อ means name/be named.
Subject omission is natural in context; ฉันชื่อแอนค่ะ remains valid.

prompt: Teach ordering one plate of non-spicy fried rice. Briefly explain the serving classifier and politeness.

expected.thai: ขอข้าวผัดหนึ่งจาน ไม่เผ็ดนะครับ
expected.english: One plate of fried rice, not spicy, please.
expected.romanization: khɔ̌ɔ khâao phàt nʉ̀ng jaan mâi phèt ná khráp

semantic_checklist: Exactly one plate; fried rice, not plain rice.
ไม่เผ็ด means not spicy, not mildly spicy.
จาน counts platefuls; ข้าว is rice, not a classifier.
นะครับ softens this request.

prompt: Teach ordering one glass of water. Explain the quantity and classifier.

expected.thai: ขอน้ำหนึ่งแก้วครับ

semantic_checklist: น้ำ is water.
หนึ่งแก้ว is one glass serving; no invented ingredients.
ขอ requests the item; not a literal ขอให้ construction.

prompt: Teach saying the nearby restroom is around here. Explain the reference point.

expected.thai: ห้องน้ำอยู่แถวนี้ค่ะ
expected.english: The restroom is around here. (Nearby-location reply.)
expected.romanization: hɔ̂ng náam yùu thɛ̌ɛo níi khâ

semantic_checklist: แถวนี้ means around here.
Do not gloss the phrase as far from here or change the reference point.

prompt: Teach saying the restroom is far from here. Explain the difference between ใกล้ and ไกล.

expected.thai: ห้องน้ำอยู่ไกลจากที่นี่ค่ะ
expected.english: The restroom is far from here. (Alternative far-location reply.)
expected.romanization: hɔ̂ng náam yùu klai jàak thîi nîi khâ

semantic_checklist: ไกล = far, mid klai; ใกล้ = near, falling klâi.
จากที่นี่ = from here, not near here.

prompt: Teach saying twenty baht. Explain the number, not two or thirty.

expected.thai: ยี่สิบบาทค่ะ

semantic_checklist: บาท is currency; ค่ะ is not part of the number.

prompt: Teach asking how much is this one, politely. Explain the question words.

expected.thai: สวัสดีค่ะ อันนี้เท่าไหร่คะ
expected.english: Hello. How much is this one?
expected.romanization: sà wàt dii khâ an níi thâo rài khá

semantic_checklist: อันนี้ = this one, not that one.
เท่าไหร่ asks how much; no invented price.
คะ is the feminine polite question ending.

prompt: Teach how to decline an offered bag and thank the seller. Explain the shopping context.

expected.thai: ไม่รับถุงค่ะ ขอบคุณค่ะ
expected.english: I won’t take a bag, thank you. (Alternative when a bag is offered.)
expected.romanization: mâi ráp thǔng khâ khɔ̀ɔp khun khâ

semantic_checklist: Declines, rather than requests, a bag.
ไม่รับ = not accepting/taking in this context; ขอบคุณ = thanks.

prompt: Teach asking do you have a bag after choosing this item. Explain the question particle.

expected.thai: เอาอันนี้ค่ะ มีถุงไหมคะ
expected.english: I’ll take this one. Do you have a bag?
expected.romanization: ao an níi khâ mii thǔng mái khá

semantic_checklist: มีถุงไหม asks availability, not a refusal.
ไหม citation mǎi vs conversational mái; คะ high khá.

prompt: Teach how to say yes politely as a confirmation. Explain the particle alternatives without claiming this answers every question.

expected.thai: ใช่ค่ะ / ใช่ครับ

semantic_checklist: ใช่ can confirm yes/correct in context.
ค่ะ / ครับ are style alternatives, not both spoken obligatorily.
Thai often answers other yes/no questions by repeating the relevant verb.

prompt: Explain คะ versus ค่ะ using the choosing-an-item and bag-question phrase. Keep citation and conversational ไหม distinct.

expected.thai: เอาอันนี้ค่ะ มีถุงไหมคะ
expected.english: I’ll take this one. Do you have a bag?
expected.romanization: ao an níi khâ mii thǔng mái khá

semantic_checklist: ค่ะ falling khâ for statement; คะ high khá for question.
ไหม citation rising mǎi; conversational high mái.
Do not call คะ rising or ค่ะ high.
